metadata.title: Add provider-specific configuration support for LLM Settings
metadata.author: kevalmahajan

description:
# 🐛 Bug-fix PR ## 📌 Summary Closes #1725 This PR fixes the LLM Settings to properly handle provider-specific configuration parameters for all LLM providers. Previously, only generic fields (API key, base URL) were supported, preventing proper configuration of providers like AWS Bedrock, IBM Watson X AI, Azure OpenAI, and Google Vertex AI that require additional provider-specific parameters. **Why this matters:** - Enables enterprise LLM providers (AWS, Azure, IBM, Google) to be properly configured - Provides type-safe validation for provider-specific parameters - Improves user experience with dynamic, context-aware forms - Eliminates configuration errors from missing required parameters ## 🔁 Reproduction Steps 1. Navigate to Admin -> LLM Settings -> Add Provider 2. Select "Azure OpenAI" as provider type 3. Observe only generic fields shown (no deployment_name, resource_name) 4. Save configuration and attempt API call 5. Call fails due to missing Azure-specific parameters ## 🐞 Root Cause **What was wrong:** 1. **Frontend**: UI only rendered static form fields, no dynamic rendering based on provider type 2. **Backend**: No validation or utilization of provider-specific configs from the `config` JSON field 3. **Proxy Service**: Hardcoded or missing provider-specific parameter extraction 4. **Missing Definitions**: No centralized definition of what each provider requires **Where:** - `mcpgateway/static/admin.js` - Static form, no dynamic field rendering - `mcpgateway/services/llm_proxy_service.py` - Incomplete provider-specific parameter usage - `mcpgateway/llm_schemas.py` - No provider-specific validation - Missing: Provider configuration definitions module ## 💡 Fix Description ### 1. **New Configuration Module** (`mcpgateway/llm_provider_configs.py`) Created centralized provider configuration definitions: - **Pydantic models** for each provider's specific requirements (AWSBedrockConfig, IBMWatsonXConfig, etc.) - **ProviderFieldDefinition**: Defines UI field properties (type, label, validation, help text, required status) - **ProviderConfigDefinition**: Complete provider configuration including all fields and metadata - **PROVIDER_CONFIGS registry**: Maps provider types to their configurations **Supported provider-specific parameters:** - **AWS Bedrock**: region, access_key_id, secret_access_key, session_token, profile_name - **IBM Watson X**: project_id, space_id, deployment_id, instance_id, version - **Azure OpenAI**: deployment_name, resource_name, api_version - **Google Vertex AI**: project_id, location, credentials_path, credentials_json - **Anthropic**: anthropic_version - **Cohere**: truncate strategy ### 2. **Backend Enhancements** **Schema Validation** (`mcpgateway/llm_schemas.py`): ```python def validate_provider_config(self) -> None: """Validate provider-specific configuration based on provider type.""" provider_def = get_provider_config(self.provider_type) for field_def in provider_def.config_fields: if field_def.required and field_def.name not in self.config: raise ValueError(f"Required field '{field_def.name}' missing") ``` **New API Endpoint** (`mcpgateway/routers/llm_admin_router.py`): ```python @llm_admin_router.get("/provider-configs") async def get_provider_configs(): """Get provider-specific configuration definitions for UI rendering.""" return {provider_type: config.model_dump() for provider_type, config in configs.items()} ``` **Enhanced Proxy Service** (`mcpgateway/services/llm_proxy_service.py`): - `_build_azure_request()`: Now extracts deployment_name, resource_name from config - `_build_anthropic_request()`: Uses anthropic_version from config - Properly utilizes provider-specific parameters when constructing API requests ### 3. **Frontend Dynamic Rendering** **Template** (`mcpgateway/templates/admin.html`): ```html
``` **JavaScript** (`mcpgateway/static/admin.js`): **New function - `renderProviderSpecificFields()`:** - Fetches provider configs from `/admin/llm/provider-configs` - Dynamically creates appropriate input elements (text, password, number, select, textarea) - Applies validation rules, placeholders, help text - Shows/hides section based on provider selection **Enhanced `onLLMProviderTypeChange()`:** - Triggers dynamic field rendering when provider type changes - Auto-fills default values for new providers **Enhanced `saveLLMProvider()`:** - Collects all `config_*` fields from dynamic form - Converts to appropriate types (number, boolean, string) - Stores in `config` object sent to backend **Enhanced `editLLMProvider()`:** - Renders provider-specific fields when editing - Populates existing config values into dynamic fields ### 4. **Key Design Decisions** **Why JSON storage:** - Leverages existing `config` JSON column in database - No schema migration required - Flexible for future provider additions - Backward compatible with existing providers **Why dynamic UI:** - Shows only relevant fields per provider - Reduces user confusion - Prevents invalid configurations - Provides contextual help **Why centralized definitions:** - Single source of truth for provider requirements - Easy to add new providers - Consistent validation across frontend/backend - Self-documenting with help text **Why Pydantic models:** - Type safety and validation - Auto-generated documentation - IDE autocomplete support - Runtime validation ## 📝 Testing **Manual Testing Performed:** - ✅ Create provider with provider-specific fields (Azure, Watson X) - ✅ Edit existing provider and modify config fields - ✅ Save and verify config stored in database - ✅ Make API calls using provider-specific configurations - ✅ Validate required field enforcement - ✅ Test field visibility when switching provider types - ✅ Verify backward compatibility with existing providers ## 🔄 Backward Compatibility ✅ **No breaking changes:** - Existing providers continue to work - `config` field already exists in database - Optional fields don't require migration - Providers without specific configs work as before ## 🧪 Verification | Check | Command | Status | |---------------------------------------|----------------------|--------| | Lint suite | `make lint` | | | Unit tests | `make test` | | | Coverage ≥ 90 % | `make coverage` | | | Manual regression no longer fails | steps / screenshots | | ## 📐 MCP Compliance (if relevant) - [x] Matches current MCP spec - [x] No breaking change to MCP clients ## ✅ Checklist - [x] Code formatted (`make black isort pre-commit`) - [x] No secrets/credentials committed
